quotes.text: Learn how to accept credit card payments using installments across a variety of Stripe products.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Installments only works with `payment` mode, not `setup` or `subscription` mode.
If you use dynamic payment methods, don’t set `payment_method_options[card][installments][enabled]`.
You must explicitly unset `payment_method_options[card][installments][plan]` when confirming the PaymentIntent again to indicate the absence of an installment plan.
You can enable installments for individual invoices but not for subscriptions.

findings: The complete 2026-11-07 canonical capture is only a variant index: it names Checkout, Elements, Direct API, Invoices and No code/Payment Links routes, with no parameters, eligibility, plans, test cards or payment outcomes (new raw lines 5-17). The 763-line older 2026-05-01 capture contains the substantive instructions for all five (old raw lines 8-763). The 768-line diff is replacement by navigation, not a demonstrated product change (diff lines 1-768).

The older Checkout variant uses payment mode only, dynamic payment methods automatically expose eligible installments, and otherwise sets card.installments.enabled in Checkout Session creation; session URL navigation is not payment success (old raw lines 18-60). Elements similarly creates a PaymentIntent, returns its client secret, and confirms with confirmPayment and return_url; issuer declines can occur (old raw lines 72-116).

The older Direct API sequence collects card details client-side through Stripe.js/Elements, creates an unconfirmed server-side PaymentIntent with a PaymentMethod ID, returns available_plans, lets the customer choose, then confirms on the server; a plan persists until explicitly unset when retrying with a different card (old raw lines 128-251, 304-487). The 2026-11-07 index merely links this variant (new raw line 15) and does not retest or renew those API and client/server details.

The older invoice variant supports individual send_invoice invoices, not charge_automatically or subscriptions; customer-configured Account and Customer identities use customer_account and customer respectively, and hosted invoice selection precedes retrieval of a selected plan from PaymentIntent (old raw lines 489-681). Older Payment Links could be toggled in Dashboard, and old sandbox card and PaymentMethod test examples include a declined Visa card (old raw lines 709-763). New raw lines 16-17 confirm only navigation to those variants.

The mapped source accurately carries a May 2026 dated digest and old raw reference (source lines 4-7, 13-46). Add the November raw as a navigation-only reference with an explicit caveat, retaining rather than silently redating the detailed May claims. Its line 19 paraphrase should use the older exact condition: with dynamic payment methods, do not set the installments.enabled field at all; false may error (old raw line 106).

Related concept and index context was checked at wiki/index.md:7, wiki/stripe-index.md:231-233, wiki/concepts/stripe-jp-installments.md:10-14,50-53, wiki/concepts/stripe-installments.md:37-49 and wiki/companies/stripe.md:469-471. Japan-account, JPY, JP-issued-credit-card and no-recurring restrictions are preserved there and in the older Japan source, but are not stated by the November variant index (wiki/sources/source-stripe-jp-installments.md:13-23).

Preserve old payment mode and send_invoice-only boundaries, dynamic-method field caveat, server-side confirmation/plan clearing and issuer-decline outcomes with their May date (old raw lines 30-32, 84-116, 200-206, 399-487, 503-526).
The old invoice examples explicitly differentiate customer-configured Account and Customer IDs (old raw lines 522-600); the November index's link does not supersede either identity path.

findings: Add the November 17-line raw as a variant-navigation reference while retaining the May 763-line raw and dated substantive guidance (source lines 4-7, 13-46; new raw lines 9-17).

source_assessments.reason: This is a navigation-format capture, not a substantive behavioral delta. The source can add its provenance and scope warning without replacing or redating the older integration details.

answers.Q1: The complete 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/jp-installments/accept-a-payment establishes only that five variants exist: Checkout, Elements, Direct API, Invoices and Payment Links; new raw lines 5-17 give links rather than requirements, code or outcomes. The older full guide documents Japan card-installment integration: Checkout payment mode, eligible card plans, client-side card capture, server-side PaymentIntent plan retrieval and confirmation, individual send_invoice invoices, and Payment Links, with test cards and declined outcomes in old raw lines 8-763. source-stripe-jp-installments-accept-payment.md accurately summarizes much of that older guide but must retain its May 2026 date when adding the November variant-index provenance. A Checkout session, available plan or invoice creation is not proof of a successful charge.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/jp-installments/accept-a-payment, the shift from a combined 763-line guide to the 17-line variant index is navigation and presentation, not proof that any integration route or parameter was removed; compare old raw lines 14-763 with new raw lines 9-17. No substantive change or reciprocal behavioral conflict is established. Keep source-stripe-jp-installments-accept-payment.md's Checkout payment-only, invoice send_invoice-only, dynamic-method, plan-clearing, Account-versus-Customer and sandbox-test claims dated to the older capture. The new links do not verify the linked variants, issuer eligibility, current UI labels or a current SDK/API version. Respect client Stripe.js and server secret-key/PaymentIntent boundaries, and distinguish plan availability, confirmation attempt, redirect and invoice delivery from succeeded payment.
